title: v1/chat.completions API surface sanity layer: param harmonization, stream stability, structured response shim
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add a compatibility and stability shim for /v1/chat.completions: parameter harmonization (aliases + explicit mapping), deterministic handling of stop/logprobs across streaming and non-streaming modes, improved streaming handshake and chunk reassembly, and structured output adapter for function/tool calls. Backwards-compatible; recommended to audit clients using raw logprob offsets.
description:
Motivation: Customers expect parity with OpenAI\u2019s /v1/chat.completions surface while retaining Redwood\u2019s production guarantees (streaming stability, deterministic stop behavior, and structured tool outputs). Over time we accumulated subtle mismatches: aliasing of role names, inconsistent stop/logprobs when a stop token is observed mid-chunk, and fragile streaming framing when tool calls interleave with role deltas. This PR introduces a lightweight compatibility layer (the "v1 surface sanity layer") that normalizes params, stabilizes stream framing, and emits a consistent structured response for function/tool calls.
Key changes (high level): 1) Param harmonizer: maps common OpenAI param names (e.g., max_tokens, presence_penalty -> presence_penalty, temperature aliases) into our internal param model, applies sane defaults, and validates conflicting params (stop + logprobs semantics). 2) Role alias normalization: accept role aliases (assistant/system/user) and historical synonyms (e.g., "bot" -> assistant) at the API boundary with deterministic precedence. 3) Stop/logprob contract: unify semantics so that when a stop token is encountered mid-stream the final token is included/excluded consistently between streaming and non-streaming modes; logprobs are adjusted to match post-truncation indexing used by OpenAI parity tests. 4) Streaming handshake and chunk reassembly: introduce a compact handshake envelope that signals model variant and active stop-mode; implement chunk sequence numbers + heartbeat sentinel to avoid reassembly corruption under intermittent TCP stalls. 5) Structured output shim for function/tool calling: ensure framed JSON chunks deliver a single top-level "function_call" object when requested and include metadata fields for tool provenance, truncated flags, and deterministic call arguments formatting. 6) Telemetry and safety gates: counters for stop-mode fallbacks, warnings for clients relying on raw token offsets, and an opt-out header (X-Redwood-Compat: legacy=false) for customers who want strict internal behavior.
Backwards compatibility and rollout: defaults preserve current behavior unless client uses /v1/chat.completions or opts into the parity mode. Safe rollout plan: staged release behind feature flag, Canary on dedicated capacity, 72h monitoring window, and automatic rollback on error rate regressions or increased truncation mismatches.
Checklist: - [x] Param mapping table and docs - [x] End-to-end streaming tests (unit + integration) - [x] Reassembly fuzz harness for chunk sequence gaps - [x] Logprob delta regression tests against OpenAI reference vectors - [x] Schema for structured function_call output and examples - [x] Docs and changelog entry - [x] Telemetry counters and alert thresholds

Look at the linked Linear tickets (ENG-3182: v1 parity plan, ENG-3210: streaming reassembly) for design sketches. This description intentionally includes examples and compatibility notes to help integrators and SDK teams migrate without surprises.

diff_summary: ~12 files changed. Param harmonizer introduces a new mapping table and ~250 LOC validation. Streaming changes add a 60-line handshake envelope and ~180 LOC reassembly with tests. Structured function_call adapter adds ~80 LOC plus example fixtures. Docs and SDK adapters updated with examples and migration snippets.
review_conversation: Marcus Liu (reviewer): High-level this looks good. Two asks: (1) make sure existing non-v1 clients are unaffected, add an explicit opt-in for strict parity; (2) clarify the logprob index adjustments in the description so SDK teams can update token offset mappings.

Ava Chen (author): Thanks Marcus. Default behavior preserved for non-/v1 endpoints; added opt-out header and explicit note in docs. Expanded logprob section with example mapping and a small conversion function in sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py.
Diego Ramirez (reviewer): Streaming reassembly code looks solid, but add a unit test for out-of-order chunk recovery + duplicate chunk dedupe. Also please add metrics for dropped chunks.
Ava Chen (author): Added test test_seq_reassembly with gap+dup scenarios and exposed a counter 'stream.reassembly.dropped_chunks' in telemetry. PTAL.

Priya Nair (reviewer): Approve after small nit: change X-Redwood-Compat header name to X-Redwood-Compat-Mode to avoid collision with other headers. Also request to include a changelog snippet for operators.
Ava Chen (author): Renamed header and added changelog snippet. Ran CI and addressed a lint complaint in openai_compat_adapter.ts.
Marcus Liu: Approved. Happy to merge once CI passes.
CI bot: All checks passed after re-run.
merge_summary: Merged feature/v1-chat-surface-sanity into main (squash). Single commit message: "v1/chat.completions: add compatibility surface, streaming stability, and structured function_call adapter". Canary held for 48h, metrics stable, rolled to general availability on 2025-08-18.
migration_notes: Clients using token offsets in logprobs should run the included SDK helper convert_logprob_offsets(old_offsets, parity_mode=True) to reconcile indices when upgrading. To opt out of parity adjustments set header X-Redwood-Compat-Mode=legacy on requests. SDKs (python/js) expose a flag openai_compat.parity_mode to toggle behavior; update CI suites that assert raw token offset positions.
testing_summary: Added regression vectors derived from OpenAI reference outputs (small sample corpus). Integration tests run on dedicated GPU canary; observed 0.3% delta in tail token timing and no user-visible truncation mismatches after adjustments. Fuzz harness found two rare reassembly cases (fixed). Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds added to detect >0.5% mismatch rate.
notes_for_sre: Feature flag: deploy/feature_flags/v1_compat.yaml controls rollout. Key alerts: stream.reassembly.dropped_chunks > 5/min, v1.stop_mismatch_rate > 0.5% over 30m, and increased 5xx rates on /v1/chat.completions. Canary timeframe: 72h recommended. Backout steps: disable v1_compat flag then rollback code if errors persist.
changelog_entry: Added v1/chat.completions parity shim: parameter harmonization, deterministic stop/logprob handling between streaming and non-streaming modes, streaming handshake robustness, and structured function_call output. Backwards-compatible; opt-out header available.
